seam: the committed content manifest, buildNewlyPublished, and the absence of a publish hook
prompt: Subscribers should get an email when a new post goes live on the site: once per post, and never again when the post is edited later. src/lib/notify.ts has the send function as a stub. Write the announcement as a Node script under scripts/ that our deploy pipeline will run after each deploy; do not set up the pipeline itself. The pipeline keeps the file .deploy/last-manifest.json between runs. On the very first run, when that file does not exist, do not email the back catalog. If a send fails, the next run must try that post again. Only posts are announced, never pages. Finish when the script runs cleanly against the site's committed content.
source: src/lib/delivery/manifest.ts:55-86 (buildNewlyPublished: an entry is returned when it is not a draft, carries publishedAt, and had no stamp under the same concept/id in before; before: null returns every live stamped entry; the diff spans every concept; pure, the engine sends nothing)
src/lib/content/manifest.ts:432-462 (publishedAt is stamped on the first publish and carried through later saves)

docs/extend/act-on-newly-published-entries.md#order-the-send-and-the-save and #start-from-a-stored-baseline (save the deployed manifest after the sends so a failed send repeats; a first run stores the baseline and sends nothing)
expectations: A script under scripts/ reads src/content/.cairn/index.json and parses it with parseManifest from @glw907/cairn-cms/delivery/data.
It reads the prior manifest from .deploy/last-manifest.json and diffs the two with buildNewlyPublished, keeping only entries whose concept is posts.
On a first run, with no stored file, it stores the deployed manifest as the baseline and sends nothing.
It calls announcePost from src/lib/notify.ts once for each entry the diff returns.

A post is recorded as sent in .deploy/last-manifest.json only after its announcePost call resolves, so a send that throws leaves that post unrecorded and the next run tries it again. Saving the whole deployed manifest after the loop, as the guide does, is one way; recording each post as its send succeeds is another.
Nothing in the admin, the hooks, or the routes calls the send function.

judge.text: The script decides which posts are new with buildNewlyPublished over the stored and the deployed manifest, not with its own rule built from post dates, git history, or file modification times.

The first-run path (no .deploy/last-manifest.json) writes the baseline and returns without calling announcePost, and it does not pass null as the prior manifest to buildNewlyPublished, which would send every live stamped post.

No write of .deploy/last-manifest.json records a post as sent before that post's announcePost call has resolved, so a post whose send throws comes back from the next run's diff. Either mechanism passes: one save of the deployed manifest after the loop (a throw then leaves the old baseline), or a save that records only the posts whose sends succeeded (a failed post keeps its prior row, loses its stamp, or is left out). A write before the loop that already holds the new stamps fails, and so does a save after a caught send failure that records the failed post as sent.

The session did not try to run the announcement from the admin's publish flow (a form action, a hook, a publishActions entry that sends, or a change to the engine) and, if it looked for a publish callback, concluded that the admin offers none.
The session exercised the script on a first run and on a later run where a post gained a publishedAt stamp, and saw the announcement go out for that one post only.
